label: Polynomial Operations
overview: Adding, subtracting, and multiplying polynomials are core algebraic skills on the SAT. Adding and subtracting require combining like terms; multiplication uses the distributive property (FOIL for two binomials). SAT questions often ask you to simplify an expression, find a specific coefficient, or match a product to one of the answer choices.

steps.title: Apply FOIL
steps.content: Multiply each term in the first binomial by each term in the second.

steps.title: Distribute the negative
steps.content: Subtraction flips all signs in the second polynomial.

commonMistakes.mistake: Forgetting to distribute the negative sign across all terms when subtracting polynomials
Adding exponents when adding like terms: x² + x² = x⁴
commonMistakes.fix: x² + x² = 2x². Coefficients add, exponents stay the same for like terms.

quickTip: For the SAT, you often only need one specific coefficient (like the x-coefficient) from a product — expand only the relevant terms to save time.
